newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends mixed, China sales press nearby.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends mixed, China sales press nearby.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed mixed with nearby March pressed by corn exports from China, traders said.
"More evidence that China is exporting corn weighed on this market," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.

Traders in Seoul said South Korea over the past week bought 76,000 tonnes of Chinese corn and in Manila, traders said the Philippines bought about 145,000 tonnes of Chinese corn. But the government declined to confirm it saying negotiations for the deal were still on.
But corn futures found strong underpinning.
Farmer selling remained slow and USDA early Tuesday released a weekly export inspections report which showed the corn tally at a level above trade expectations.
Also fund buying and fund short covering continued at a steady pace, the traders said. "They (funds) are getting positioned for our (U.S.) weather market," a trader said.
Commercial buying boosted new crop December. Cargill Inc bought 4.5 million bushels of December and Tenco Inc sold five million bushels of March, the traders said.
Corn closed 1/2 cent per bushel lower to 1-1/4 higher, with March down 1/2 at $2.70-1/2.
Tenco Inc sold five million bushels of March and Refco Inc sold 1.0 million March, 1.5 million May and 1.5 million July, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 46,000 contracts, above the 44,900 traded Tuesday, traders said.
In corn options, Farmes Commodities Corp bought 1,000 December $2.60 puts and sold 1,000 December $3.10 calls at 7-3/4 to eight cents, traders said.
FIMAT Futures sold 800 March $2.60 calls and sold 800 March $2.60 puts at 13 to 13-1/4 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, about the same as the 15,220 traded Tuesday.
